title: Morning Edition
intro: The top line: New Gemini tools for small business owners. Here are the stories worth your time right now, pulled from 116 newsrooms and labs.

items.title: New Gemini tools for small business owners
items.summary: We’re announcing new tools for Gemini — including a dedicated business landing page — to help small business owners around the world.
items.why: This is AI showing up in ordinary businesses, not just at the big labs.

items.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to build AI agents that speed up drug development
items.summary: OpenAI is acquiring startup Orchestra Bio and plans to merge it with its life sciences AI platform Rosalind. The goal is to build AI agents that help pharma teams coordinate drug development, from tracking trials to spotting problems. Developing a new drug in the US takes ten to 15 years on average. OpenAI already works with Novo Nordisk and Moderna on AI-driven pharma research. The article OpenAI acquires Orchestra
items.why: Where the money goes shows which AI businesses investors think will last.

top.title: Claude Science tackles deadly scorpion stings by designing protein binders from scratch
top.summary: Anthropic's Claude independently designed protein binders targeting deadly scorpion neurotoxins. Out of more than 318,000 designs, 211 were tested in the lab. Seventeen met the criteria, and the two strongest bind extremely tightly to Cn2, a toxin from a Mexican scorpion. Whether they actually work as antivenom remains an open question.
